audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.quote: Use this flow when you want to create an on-demand snapshot from a node
snapshot_auto.note: No save-on-stop/idle behaviour documented; nodes are plain VMs whose disk persists. Optional 'Scheduled Snapshots' ("Where supported, you can schedule snapshots for a node and selected attached volumes.") and separate CDP Backups are time-based, not stop-triggered.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of node storage. Use snapshots when you need a restore point for node disks or attached volumes.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Disk only (root disk + selected attached volumes), no memory. 'Snapshot Now' in console; snapshot can be 'Save as Image' and new nodes created from a saved image (fork/template). C3/SDC3/M3 etc. can Save Image while Running ('the node does not need to be powered off first'). Availability depends on node family; GPU nodes: 'no snapshots' per GPU index (Save Image instead).

harness_api.note: E2E's public REST API surface (MyAccount API, TIR container-registry API) only covers plain VM/node lifecycle, GPU nodes, storage, networking, and their container-registry product. No agent-harness / AI-agent-sandbox API endpoint exists anywhere in the docs index (llms.txt) or API reference — E2E is a general-purpose hyperscaler VM/GPU cloud, not an agent-sandbox platform, so the feature is plainly outside what the product is.

egress_allowlist.quote: 2. **Outbound Rule** – Defines which traffic is allowed to leave your resource.
egress_allowlist.note: Security Groups (E2E-managed, applied 'before traffic reaches the node operating system'); rules by protocol (ALL/TCP/UDP), port list, IPv4 CIDR/any/VPC. No hostnames. 'At least one inbound rule and one outbound rule must be configured.'

egress_http_rules.quote: The Security Group then decides which types of traffic are allowed, based on protocol, port numbers, and source IP addresses and blocks everything else.
egress_http_rules.note: L3/L4 only on nodes. (ALB has L7 ACLs but that is ingress load balancing.)

ingress_rules.quote: 1. **Inbound Rule** – Defines which traffic is allowed to enter your resource (who can access your resource).
ingress_rules.note: Security group inbound rules by protocol/port/source IP (incl. 'My IP / Whitelist IP'); VPC private networking available.

guest_firewall.quote: confirm the node's OS firewall (iptables, firewalld, Windows Firewall) is not dropping the traffic.
guest_firewall.note: Full KVM VM with root; docs refer to the node's own OS firewall.

secret_proxy.quote: E2E Secrets Management provides a secure, dedicated secret store instance per customer team or application.
secret_proxy.note: Only a Vault-compatible (OpenBao) secret store the VM reads from; no credential-injecting egress proxy.

volume_attach.quote: E2E Volume provides block-level storage volumes to use with our compute nodes. These volumes can be attached to your computing nodes, making their data and file system available for your nodes.
volume_attach.note: Supported on GPU, vGPU, SDC, SDC3, C3 and Windows (CW/WSDC) nodes only. Single-node attach implied (attach flow selects one node); not stated explicitly.

volume_shared.quote: It allows multiple E2E Nodes to access the same file system concurrently, enabling shared file storage across instances.
volume_shared.note: Scalable File System (SFS) = managed NFS within a VPC, per-node ACL permissions (read-write; per-node permission choice). Also EPFS (Lustre parallel FS, 'Supports multiple simultaneous clients').

isolation.quote: Some portal labels still use category names such as Linux Virtual Node, Windows Virtual Node, Linux Smart Dedicated Compute, and Windows Smart Dedicated Compute.
isolation.note: derived: nodes are full 'Virtual Node' VMs with root/guest-firewall access on a shared multi-tenant cloud; exact hypervisor name (KVM) not published on official pages.

image_oci.quote: A saved image is a reusable image created from a node. Use it when you want to launch another node from the same configured operating system and software state.
image_oci.note: not offered: node images are OS-level VM disk images captured from an existing node, not user-supplied Docker/OCI images used to boot a machine.

docker_inside.note: Docker (plus NVIDIA Container Toolkit for GPU nodes) is documented to run inside nodes; full root VM.

browser.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (plain IaaS VM/GPU cloud, not a browser/agent sandbox product).

computer_use.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
computer_use.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

anti_bot.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

captcha_solving.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

egress_ip_type.quote: Outbound Rule – Defines which traffic is allowed to leave your resource.
egress_ip_type.note: derived: ordinary datacenter-hosted cloud VM egress IPs; no residential/mobile IP product offered.

fork.quote: Saved Images area | View saved images created from nodes and use them to create new nodes.
fork.note: Save Image from a node, then launch new nodes from that saved image.

fork_running.quote: C3/SDC3/M3 etc. can Save Image while Running ("the node does not need to be powered off first").
fork_running.note: Quote is paraphrased from prior card research (feature_evidence.snapshot_on_demand) citing this same page; source node does not need to stop while its image is captured, but the resulting clone is a new, separately started node.

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: A snapshot is a point-in-time copy of node storage. Use snapshots when you need a restore point for node disks or attached volumes.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Snapshots/saved images capture disk only; no running-process/memory state is captured or restored.

pause_resume.quote: Compute billing | Continues. | Pauses for stopped-node.
pause_resume.note: Stop deallocates the node and pauses compute billing (storage/IPs/etc. can keep billing); Start resumes it.

wake_on_request.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
wake_on_request.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; nodes are plain VMs started/stopped explicitly, not woken automatically by inbound requests.

auto_stop_idle.quote: Use Stop where the portal supports deallocating the node from the underlying host.
auto_stop_idle.note: not offered: Stop/Power Off are explicit user/API actions; no documented idle-triggered auto-stop for nodes.

live_resize.quote: Wait for the portal to return to the compute page and for the node status to settle.
live_resize.note: Plan upgrade is a distinct guided action (select target plan, confirm, wait for status to settle); no documented in-place CPU/RAM change on a still-running node without this process, and for non-E1 series a downgrade afterward is explicitly disallowed.

agent_harnesses.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
agent_harnesses.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; Marketplace images are OS/software templates, not coding-agent harnesses.

own_agent_api.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
own_agent_api.note: not offered: outside the product's scope.

mcp_server.quote: Landing page for all REST APIs, with category cards and downloadable OpenAPI specs.
mcp_server.note: Only a plain REST/OpenAPI surface is documented; no MCP server for controlling nodes found.

lang_python.quote: a base-image recommendation table (verification, CUDA dev, PyTorch, TensorFlow, vLLM, TGI)
lang_python.note: Standard Linux OS images (Ubuntu/Rocky/etc.) and documented Python-based ML workflows (PyTorch/TensorFlow/vLLM) imply Python availability; not a distinct 'language runtime' product claim.

public_ipv4.quote: Configure VPC and Public IP, Configure Public IPv4, Review Security Group, Add SSH Keys
public_ipv4.note: Create-node flow has an explicit Public IPv4 configuration step.

inbound_https.quote: choosing between an Application Load Balancer (ALB, Layer 7, HTTP/HTTPS, ACL routing, HTTP health checks, auto scaling backends) ... HTTPS via imported SSL certificates
inbound_https.note: ALB provides HTTPS ingress to node backends; ports can also be exposed directly via public IP + security group.

static_egress_ip.quote: Outbound Rule – Defines which traffic is allowed to leave your resource.
static_egress_ip.note: not offered: security groups control outbound traffic by IP/port/protocol, but no documented fixed/static outbound IP or NAT-gateway product; the node's own public/private IP is the egress source.

macos.note: not offered: outside the product's scope; only Linux and Windows node categories are offered, no macOS.

arm64.note: not offered: all published node/GPU/SDC/E1 sizes are conventional x86 vCPU SKUs; no ARM/Graviton/Ampere family found in pricing or docs.

self_host.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
self_host.note: not offered: E2E Cloud is a hosted multi-tenant cloud service, not distributed software to self-host.

byoc.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
byoc.note: not offered: capacity runs in E2E's own Indian datacenters; no bring-your-own-cloud-account deployment model documented.

open_source.quote: India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider, offering high-performance GPU computing, enterprise cloud solutions, and managed services for AI and ML workloads.
open_source.note: not offered: MyAccount/TIR platform is proprietary; no OSI-licensed core product identified.

soc2.quote: Our Certifications SOC 2 (Public Report) Application and management of security controls
soc2.note: Listed as a downloadable certification alongside ISO 27001:2022, ISO 27018:2019, ISO 27017:2015, PCI DSS, ISO 9001:2015, ISO 20000-1:2018.

hipaa.quote: Our Certifications SOC 2 (Public Report) ... ISO 27001:2022 ... ISO 27018:2019 ... ISO 27017:2015 ... PCI DSS ... ISO 9001:2015 ... ISO 20000-1:2018
hipaa.note: not offered: the certifications page lists SOC 2/ISO/PCI DSS but no HIPAA eligibility or BAA is mentioned anywhere on official pages found.

sso.quote: Platform: API Tokens, License Management, Billing, Settings, Tags, Event Monitoring, Secret Management, SSO.
sso.note: SSO is listed as its own MyAccount API resource/tag; exact SAML/OIDC details not further detailed in the indexes reviewed.

max_session_h.quote: Use Stop where the portal supports deallocating the node from the underlying host.
max_session_h.note: Pay-as-you-go nodes are ordinary VMs that run until the customer stops/deletes them; no documented maximum session duration or forced shutdown.

desktop.quote: This tutorial will explain to you how to install and configure the Xrdp on Ubuntu 18.04. ... Step 3: Install your preferred desktop environment ... To install XFCE Please use below command: sudo apt-get install xfce4
desktop.note: E2E nodes ship as plain Linux/Windows VMs with no desktop/GUI preinstalled. The official guide for remote-desktop access requires the customer to manually install xrdp plus a desktop environment (XFCE or MATE) themselves — confirming no first-party desktop is offered out of the box.

eu_data_residency.quote: India's GPU Cloud for AI ... India's leading GPU cloud infrastructure provider for AI & ML workloads
eu_data_residency.note: E2E Networks is an Indian sovereign-cloud provider headquartered in Delhi, India; its own card lists only the "asia" region for every compute product line, and no EU/European data-center or residency option is advertised anywhere on the official site or docs. Plainly outside what the product is (India-only cloud, no EU presence).
